articles.headline: OFAC Designates Guatemalan Drug Trafficking Organizations for Narcotics and Terrorism
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on November 13, 2026, targeting several Guatemalan drug trafficking organizations under its Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism sanctions programs. The designated entities include LOS LORENZANAS (also known as LORENZANA DRUG TRAFFICKING ORGANIZATION, THE LORENZANA CLAN, and THE LORENZANA FAMILY), LOS MENDOZA DRUG TRAFFICKING ORGANIZATION, and LOS HUISTAS DRUG TRAFFICKING ORGANIZATION.

These organizations are identified as transnational terrorist groups and criminal organizations, with LOS MENDOZA and LOS HUISTAS specifically linked to the SINALOA CARTEL and CARTEL DE JALISCO NUEVA GENERACION. The designations carry secondary sanctions risks under Executive Order 13224, as amended by Executive Order 13886, and Executive Order 14059.

The action aims to disrupt the financial networks and operations of these groups, which play a significant role in illicit drug trafficking and pose a threat to regional stability. This move underscores the U.S. government's ongoing efforts to combat international narcotics trafficking and terrorism.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran Designation Update
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an Iran Designation Update on November 9, 2026. This action signifies ongoing adjustments and additions to the Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List related to Iran.

While specific details of the updated designations were not immediately released in a separate press statement, such updates typically target individuals or entities involved in proliferation, terrorism, or other activities deemed detrimental to U.S. national security and foreign policy objectives concerning Iran.

These regular updates are part of OFAC's comprehensive strategy to maintain pressure on the Iranian regime and its affiliates, aiming to prevent illicit financial activities and support for destabilizing actions.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces New Iran-related Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on November 6, 2026. These actions are part of the ongoing effort to counter the Iranian regime's destabilizing activities.
The designations aim to target individuals and entities that support Iran's illicit activities, including its nuclear program, ballistic missile development, and support for terrorism.
These measures reinforce existing sanctions regimes and seek to further isolate those involved in facilitating the Iranian government's problematic behaviors.

articles.headline: OFAC Sanctions Cyber, Transnational Criminal Organizations, and Cuba-Related Entities; Publishes Cuba Determination
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a series of designations on November 5, 2026, targeting cyber-related actors, transnational criminal organizations, and entities linked to Cuba. This action includes the publication of a Cuba-related Determination Pursuant to Section 2(a)(i)(A) of Executive Order 14404, specifically focusing on the 'Electronics, Manufacturing, Marine, and Technology Sectors of the Cuban Economy.'

Among the individuals added to OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List are Kok Wa Chui from Madagascar, and Yujing He, Visal Pang, and Yong Qiu, all with connections to Cambodia and identified with the PRINCE GROUP TRANSNATIONAL CRIMINAL ORGANIZATION. Additionally, Any Rodriguez Lastres from Panama City, Cuba, was designated.

These designations aim to disrupt global scam networks and the corporate infrastructure that enables them, as well as to further restrict the Cuban regime's foreign military support and illicit revenue networks. The action underscores the U.S. commitment to combating cybercrime, transnational criminal activities, and supporting human rights in Cuba.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-related Designations, Alert on Shadow Fleet, and Amends Venezuela GL
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on November 4, 2026, alongside updates to certain Iran-related listings. This action also included the publication of an Iran-related OFAC Alert titled 'Iranian Shadow Fleet Reliance on False Flags for Sanctions Evasion,' and the issuance of an amended Venezuela-related General License and Frequently Asked Question.

The Iran-related designations added several entities to OFAC's SDN List, including ALEXARYA FINSERV PRIVATE LIMITED, ALEXARYA MEDIA AND ENTERTAINMENT PRIVATE LIMITED, POLYNESIA MARITIME PRIVATE LIMITED, PRECEPT TRENDS PRIVATE LIMITED, ARYAVART MARITIME AND EDUCATIONAL TRUST, and ARYAVART SHIP MANAGEMENT PRIVATE LIMITED, all based in India and linked to Jaspreet Preeti Shahid. These entities face secondary sanctions risk under Executive Order 13902.

Furthermore, OFAC issued Venezuela-related General License 5AA, 'Authorizing Certain Transactions Related to the Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. 2020 8.5 Percent Bond on or After December 18, 2026,' and amended FAQ 595. The Iran-related alert provides crucial guidance on deceptive shipping practices used to evade sanctions, highlighting the U.S. government's focus on maritime enforcement.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-related General License FF-1
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the issuance of Iran General License FF-1 on October 29, 2026. This amended general license is titled 'Authorizing the Wind Down of Transactions Involving International Development Bank for Investment and Finance.'

General License FF-1 provides a specific authorization for the wind-down of transactions, indicating a period during which certain activities with the International Development Bank for Investment and Finance can be concluded without incurring sanctions violations.
This action is part of OFAC's ongoing management of sanctions programs, providing clarity and a structured approach for entities to divest or cease operations with sanctioned parties.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Sanctions North Korea and DRC-Related Entities, Individuals for IT Worker Fraud and M23 Support
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on October 28, 2026, targeting individuals and entities connected to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). These actions address DPRK IT worker fraud and support for the M23 rebel group in the DRC.

Among the North Korea-related designations, OFAC added Russian national Ilya Aleksandrovich Boykov, and North Korean nationals Han Yu Song and Ri Thae Chol, all linked to Russia. Entities designated include FIRST FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENT CENTER, CHINYONG INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY COOPERATION COMPANY, and LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY ALIS, with listed digital currency addresses on Ethereum and TRON.

The DRC-related designations include the Rwandan Ministry of Defence and Zigama Credit and Savings Society (Zigama CSS), a Kigali-based financial institution, for their alleged support of the M23. These measures aim to disrupt illicit financial activities and destabilizing actions in both regions.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks Settles with OFAC for $1.5 Million Over Russia Sanctions Violations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc., a North Carolina-headquartered cloud networking solutions provider, on October 27, 2026. Extreme Networks agreed to pay $1,529,685 to resolve nine apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.

Between September 2018 and March 2022, Extreme Networks exported networking equipment and related services from the United States to Joint Stock Company (JSC) Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA), a Russian defense manufacturer. MMZA was deemed a blocked person by operation of law due to its majority ownership by the designated JSC Concern Almaz Antey, even though MMZA itself was not directly listed on the SDN List until June 2022.

OFAC determined that the apparent violations were voluntarily self-disclosed and egregious. The settlement amount reflects this, and Extreme Networks has committed to maintaining a robust sanctions compliance program for at least five years, including enhanced screening procedures and annual executive certification. The Department of Justice also resolved a parallel investigation.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Filing Reports
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced on October 26, 2026, that it is amending several Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) as part of its ongoing review of published guidance. This update focuses on FAQs related to blocking and rejecting transactions and on filing reports with OFAC.

The amended FAQs (numbers 10, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 41, 42, 49, 50, and 53) aim to ensure that information remains current and provides clearer explanations for financial institutions and other entities regarding their obligations under U.S. sanctions programs. Key areas covered include when to block versus reject a transaction, interest requirements on blocked funds, and the timing and procedures for reporting blocked property and rejected transactions through the OFAC Reporting System.

While these amendments do not introduce new sanctions programs or designations, they are crucial for compliance teams to review to ensure their internal procedures align with OFAC's latest guidance, particularly concerning the correct handling and reporting of sanctions-related transactions.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-related Designations, Belarus and North Korea Removals, and New General Licenses
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a series of actions on October 21, 2026, including new Iran-related designations, removals of certain Belarus and North Korea designations, and the issuance of Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses. Additionally, OFAC published amended Frequently Asked Questions.

These actions reflect OFAC's dynamic approach to sanctions, adjusting measures based on evolving geopolitical landscapes and compliance needs. The Iran-related designations aim to further pressure the Iranian regime, while the removals from the Belarus and North Korea lists may indicate specific policy adjustments or compliance by previously designated entities.

The issuance of new General Licenses for Iran and Russia, along with updated FAQs, provides important guidance for businesses and individuals navigating complex sanctions environments, ensuring clarity on permissible transactions and reporting requirements.

body: Extreme Networks, Inc. has paid a civil penalty of $1,529,685 to the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). This settlement resolves apparent violations of U.S. sanctions regulations.

The case highlights the importance of thorough due diligence, especially in mergers and acquisitions, to identify and prevent dealings with entities that are blocked under OFAC's 50 percent rule, even if they are not explicitly listed on the SDN List.

articles.headline: China Expresses 'Serious Concern' Over New US Sanctions Ahead of Trade Talks
body: China has voiced 'serious concern' over recent U.S. sanctions targeting Chinese companies, ahead of a new round of trade negotiations and a potential meeting between Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump at the APEC summit in Shenzhen. Chinese Vice-Premier He Lifeng held a video conference with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer to discuss key trade issues.

China's Ministry of Commerce 'firmly opposes' the latest sanctions imposed by the U.S. government on two Chinese companies, stating that these measures 'undermine the stability of bilateral economic and trade relations.' The Ministry urged the U.S. to correct its 'wrongful practices as soon as possible' and reserved the right to take necessary measures to safeguard its legitimate rights and interests.

The U.S. State Department announced sanctions against China National Electronic Import and Export Company (CEIEC) and Beijing H&C Technologies for allegedly supplying military-related goods to Cuba in 2026. Additionally, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) voted to ban all Chinese laboratories from testing electronic devices destined for the U.S. market, effective December 2028.

articles.headline: Revisions to the Entity List
body: In this rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) revises the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by removing two addresses associated with Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. from the Entity List under the destination of China, People's Republic of (China). This determination follows the removal from the Entity List of Arrow China Electronics Trading Co., Ltd., and the removal of six aliases for Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. in November 2025.

articles.headline: Removal From the Entity List
body: In this rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by removing one entity from the Entity List under the destination of Turkey.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
